title: Graceful stall detection and tenant quiet-mode + customer escalation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer reports elevated 5xx/timeouts originating from a combination of long-lived streaming connections and bursty tenant uploads. This ticket scopes an immediate mitigation (tenant quiet-mode + conservative admission control) and a corresponding production bugfix to stop request-retry amplification and KV cache thrashing during tenant surges.
impact_summary: Multiple enterprise customers observed sustained 5xx spikes, increased tail latency, and replay-amplified retries for ~30 minutes on 2026-03-09. Some customers reported degraded UX and opened escalations with support. Estimated affected tenants: 12, top-3 customers saw 2–4x error rates.
root_cause_summary: Investigation shows a cascade of conditions: (1) large multipart uploads interleaved with long-lived streams cause edge proxy connection exhaustion; (2) aggressive SDK/client retries amplify request rates; (3) KV cache eviction thrash under sudden working set shifts leads to higher inference runtime coldstarts and increased 5xxs. No single fix is sufficient without coordination between admission control and KV eviction smoothing.
mitigation:
1) Roll out tenant quiet-mode: temporarily place affected tenants into a degraded admission profile that rejects non-critical requests with clear 429/503 guidance and reduces client-side retries.
2) Edge proxy tuning: increase connection pool headroom and add early-abort for slow multipart uploads.
3) Short-term KV cache compaction pause for nodes under >80% eviction churn to avoid cascading cold starts.
4) Customer comms: send proactive status and recommended client-side backoff configuration.
Mitigation rollout began 2026-03-10 15:20 UTC; initial telemetry shows error rate drop of ~60% for targeted tenants.
workaround: Advise customers to (a) disable aggressive client SDK auto-retry during incident windows, (b) limit multipart chunk concurrency, (c) temporarily reduce streaming keepalive durations. Support playbook attached.
resolution: Implement admission controller that supports tenant quiet-mode + edge proxy soft-abort and KV compaction gating. Follow-up bugfix to correct socket-count misreporting in proxy (root cause of pool mis-sizing). Plan for staged rollout to dedicated and private fleets after validation.
rollback_plan: If quiet-mode causes unacceptable customer impact, revert tenant to normal admission and enable graceful throttling (per-tenant leaky-bucket) for 1 hour while further fixes are deployed. All rollouts are gated behind feature-flag and can be rolled back via console or feature-flag API.
acceptance_criteria: Error rate for previously impacted tenants reduced to <= 1.2x baseline within 1 hour of rollout
No increase in streaming latency > 10% for gold-tier tenants during rollout
Edge proxy socket pool metrics show correct sizing and <5% headroom exhaustion across regions
KV cache eviction churn reduced to <30% peak compared to incident baseline
Support playbook and customer communications drafted, reviewed by PS and Comms
tasks: Add tenant quiet-mode flag to admission-controller (feature flag behind runtime:quiet_mode)
Implement KV compaction gating to pause aggressive compaction during eviction surges (PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2196)
Create observability dashboards: tenant-quiet-mode, admission-rejects, kv-eviction-churn
Run canary in us-west2 with 3 tenants for 2 hours, collect telemetry
Draft and send customer escalation email template (owner: Support lead)
